question: Which of the following plantations helps in the prevention of soil erosion in desert?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shelter belts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Shelter belts are rows of trees or shrubs planted to protect an area from strong winds and erosion.
 
• These belts help in reducing the velocity of the wind, which prevents soil erosion in desert areas.
 
• They act as barriers that trap moving soil particles and reduce the amount of soil transported by wind.
 
• Shelter belts also improve the microclimate of the area, making it more suitable for other vegetation and agricultural activities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Agroforestry**

 
 
• Agroforestry involves integrating trees and shrubs into agricultural landscapes to enhance biodiversity, reduce erosion, and improve soil health.
 
• While beneficial for soil conservation, it is not specifically designed for preventing soil erosion in desert areas.
 
 
 
• **Strip Cropping**
 
 
• Strip cropping involves growing crops in strips or bands to reduce soil erosion and improve soil fertility.
 
• This technique is more commonly used in hilly or sloped areas rather than deserts.
 
 
 
• **Contour Ploughing**
 
 
• Contour ploughing is the practice of ploughing along the contour lines of a slope to reduce soil erosion.
 
• It is particularly effective in hilly and sloped regions but not specifically designed for desert areas.
